signals.title: NZD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Policy Divergence
signals.text: NZD leads the G10 currency dashboard with a 1W average gain of +0.923% across 4 pairs, while NOK lags at −1.000% across 2 pairs, establishing a 1.923% spread that triggers the critical bilateral threshold. The move decouples from nominal rates where Norges Bank holds at 4.5% against the RBNZ at 2.75%, leaving NZD with a 175bp nominal policy deficit. Meanwhile, NZ 2Y yield spreads vs US have widened +14bp over 5 sessions to −75bp, whereas Norway's 2s10s curve sits inverted at −22bp. The divergence reflects heavy cross-currency momentum favoring NZD despite persistent negative domestic data surprises shown in an ESI of −25.1. Trade bias: Long NZD/NOK, momentum-driven bilateral extension. Catalyst: Norges Bank Financial Stability Report at 07:30 UTC. Risk: Spread compresses below 1.20% as oil softness drags broader commodity risk.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + BoJ Summary
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.98, capped directly below its SMA20 of 157.93 and SMA200 of 158.59 within a tight 20-session box. 25-delta risk reversals register at −2.05, signaling extreme put skew and persistent demand for downside hedging protection. Overnight BoJ Summary of Opinions confirmed hawkish pressure among board members pushing for faster rate hikes toward a neutral rate above 1%. A 266bp OIS carry advantage favors USD via SOFR at 3.89% vs TONA at 1.23%, sustaining the base of the pair while implied vol runs at 6.7% against HV30 of 4.9% for a +1.8% premium. With 160.00 remaining the key level that has previously triggered intervention warnings, the downside skew highlights structural wariness over official action and policy repricing. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY, heavy downside options hedging against carry support. Catalyst: BoJ L Money Stock release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: A daily close above the SMA200 at 158.59 that forces put-skew unwinds.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1225, holding above its SMA20 of 1.1198 but remaining trapped beneath the SMA50 at 1.1339 and SMA200 at 1.1546. CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds net short −104,030 contracts at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of −1.80, marking an extreme institutional short position. Meanwhile, 1-month ATM IV sits at 5.7% against realized HV30 of 5.1%, reflecting a subdued 0.6% vol risk premium and muted put demand via 25d RR at −0.30. Macro carry structurally anchors the pair, with Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% yielding a 135bp spread favoring USD alongside a SOFR-€STR OIS advantage of 145bp. Given the exhausted spec short positioning, the pair faces asymmetric squeeze risk on any US disinflation print. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD mean reversion, short-squeeze setup against crowded institutional shorts. Catalyst: US CPI release at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Sustained break below the SMA20 at 1.1198 following a hotter-than-forecast US CPI print.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Downtrend Structure + Macro Headwinds
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6923, holding in an established downtrend with its 20-day moving average falling below the 200-day line while price sits beneath the SMA20 of 0.6990 and SMA50 of 0.7043. Overnight domestic releases showed NAB business conditions dropping to six-year lows and consumer sentiment hitting four-year troughs, reinforcing expectations for an RBA pause. RBA policy rate at 4.85% vs Fed at 4.00% maintains an 85bp carry premium for AUD, reinforced by an AONIA-SOFR OIS spread of 96bp. However, the options market maintains downside protection demand, with AUD/USD 25d RR at −1.30 while CFTC Leveraged Funds hold a net long position of +43,532 contracts. This leaves stale institutional longs vulnerable to liquidation as domestic macro data softens. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, trend-continuation setup against weakening domestic fundamentals. Catalyst: Fed Governor Waller speech at 09:00 UTC. Risk: A daily close through the SMA20 at 0.6990 invalidating immediate downward momentum.
